name: Familial Spontaneous Pneumothorax

criteria.description: Presence of spontaneous pneumothorax in two or more first-degree relatives
Recurrent episodes of spontaneous pneumothorax without apparent cause
Exclusion of secondary causes such as trauma, lung disease, or iatrogenic factors
Presence of subpleural blebs or bullae on chest imaging
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with familial pneumothorax (e.g., FLCN gene mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two major criteria including family history and recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax, with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

imaging: High-resolution CT scan revealing subpleural blebs or bullae
other: Exclusion of secondary causes by clinical and laboratory evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: Usually occurs in tall, thin young males without genetic predisposition
Underlying lung disease such as COPD, cystic fibrosis, or infections
Often older patients with known pulmonary pathology

redFlags: Sudden severe chest pain with respiratory distress
Signs of tension pneumothorax (hypotension, tracheal deviation)
Recurrent pneumothorax episodes in multiple family members
references: Birt AR, Hogg GR, Dubé WJ. Hereditary multiple fibrofolliculomas with trichodiscomas and acrochordons. Arch Dermatol. 1977.
Sahn SA, Heffner JE. Spontaneous pneumothorax. N Engl J Med. 2000.
